triggers.when: Archiving a Spec under normal QA eligibility or an explicitly user-authorized QA Archive Override, with non-QA Tasks completed.
Starting creative feature or behavior design before implementation.
Evaluating product viability, options, KPIs, or business trade-offs.
Defining or changing domain vocabulary, ownership, or bounded-context relationships.
When the person asks to stress-test a plan or decision against repository documents.
Stress-testing an idea or plan through direct questions.
Executing exactly one assigned Spec Task.
Delegating one autonomous Task to an ACP Runtime.
Consulting the configured knowledge workspace for relevant prior context.
Consulting the Secondbrain before authoring an Idea, PRD, or TechSpec.
Running final Spec QA after implementation Tasks complete.
Auditing or applying the Context-Driven Baseline for first adoption, or refreshing an adopted repository with `roundfix baseline update`.
Expanding a product-level idea into a researched opportunity artifact.
Defining product requirements and user outcomes.
Decomposing an approved Spec into a dependency-ordered Task Graph.
Settling implementation architecture and technical contracts.

clauses.guidance: The repository's selected domain context and its accepted ADRs are the base of the CONTEXT-driven workflow. Read both before naming domain concepts or changing behavior, and flag conflicts instead of silently overriding repository decisions.

Use the repository's canonical domain terms in code names, tests, user-facing copy, Specs, and delivery notes. In a code name, a term takes its Name in Code: the term itself, or the name its Glossary Definition records on a line `_In code_:` when the term was translated to English or kept without accents. A Spec that introduces or changes such a term writes that line. Call out a missing term instead of inventing a competing synonym.
Follow the repository's declared single-context or multi-context layout. Setup can require that decision but cannot infer bounded contexts from directory names.

A Spec adds each domain term it introduces to the domain context, and revises each term it changes, through `domain-modeling` in one of its own Tasks, whose Verification names the term. It lists those terms in a `## Glossary` section of its PRD or TechSpec, with any bolded phrase it declares not a domain term. `roundfix spec check` reports a bolded term the domain context lacks and the section does not cover, and the QA gate and `roundfix archive` refuse a Spec whose declared term is still missing. When `domain-modeling` names its glossary file differently, it writes to the selected domain context. Work outside a Spec checks at its close whether it introduced, changed, or retired a term and updates the domain context when it did. Neither the check nor the update waits for human interaction; reach for `grilling` only when a term is ambiguous enough to need sharpening before it is written down.

When creating a new ADR, prepend this repository-owned lifecycle overlay to the body contract in `.agents/skills/domain-modeling/ADR-FORMAT.md`:

```markdown
---
status: proposed # proposed | accepted | rejected | deprecated | superseded
created_at: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
updated_at: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
deprecated_at: null # null or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
superseded_by: null # null or ADR-NNNN
---

# <Short title of the decision>

<One to three sentences describing the context, decision, and reason.>
```

An accepted ADR that a later accepted ADR changes in part, without replacing it, stays `accepted`. In the change that adds the later ADR, its header gains `amended_by: [ADR-NNNN]`, and its body gains, after the text that changed, a dated notice that begins `Amended by ADR-NNNN (YYYY-MM-DD)` and says what changed. `roundfix baseline update` fills the list from the notices an ADR already carries.
For an ADR that carries lifecycle frontmatter, only `accepted` is active. Treat `proposed`, `rejected`, `deprecated`, and `superseded` ADRs as inactive.

Treat a legacy ADR without lifecycle frontmatter as active unless its body explicitly marks it inactive. Do not rewrite existing ADRs solely to adopt lifecycle metadata. The one exception is a header field that a guide of this repository defines for existing ADRs, such as `amended_by`: it is written into them and changes no other line, and a header that holds no lifecycle field leaves its ADR a legacy ADR.

Give each documentation directory one job: `docs/_inbox/` for raw notes only when a repository has no Secondbrain, `docs/adr/` for decisions, `docs/agents/` for agent guidance, `docs/design/` for design artifacts of the product, such as an interface, API or data design, and never a decision or a plan, `docs/backlog/` for dated, typed intent not yet committed to a Spec, `docs/findings/` for dated investigations, `docs/handoffs/` for session continuity, `docs/lessons/` for Lessons Learned, `docs/references/` for external pointers and durable project reference documents, including one that would otherwise sit at the repository root, the `DESIGN.md` design contract excepted, and `docs/user-guide/` for human documentation. A folder under `docs/` or a reference document at the root that this clause does not name is a variation: name its path and its job in `docs/agents/specific-repository.md`, or move its content to the directory whose job it is. `roundfix doctor` reports one that is neither. Preserve repository-authored bytes outside setup markers, and add a repository rule only to `docs/agents/specific-repository.md`. Each directory holds live work only. The history root `docs/history/` holds Archive Records, and Git keeps their full text. Spec-contained authorization records live at `<spec-root>/<slug>/_authorization.md`; the preserved legacy location `docs/workflow/authorizations/` remains readable for historical grants. When the runtime's archive leaves an Archive Record, the record names each Spec-owned adopted reference, and the reference leaves the tree with the Spec folder.

Durable knowledge flows upstream only: the project glossary (`CONTEXT.md`) and the agent guides reference accepted ADRs and never reference `docs/specs/` or `docs/findings/` content. Findings are dated reports that become Specs, not reference material; a document meant as durable project reference belongs in `docs/references/`.

Name backlog entries `YYYY-MM-DD-<kebab-slug>.md`. Use this complete copyable Backlog Operational Contract:

```markdown
---
type: feat # feat | fix | perf | refactor
status: open # open | promoted | declined | deferred | done | deprecated | superseded | closed | cancelled
created: YYYY-MM-DD
spec: null # Spec slug when status: promoted
reason: null # required for terminal closure without a consuming Spec
# waiting_on: <who or what it waits on, in one line> # optional, with since
# since: YYYY-MM-DD # optional, the date the wait began
---
```

An `open` entry that waits on someone or something outside the repository may uncomment `waiting_on`, naming who or what in one line, and `since`, the `YYYY-MM-DD` date the wait began.

For `type: feat`, use:

```markdown
# <Title — the intent in one line>

## Opportunity

<What could exist and for whom.>

## Value

<Why it would matter; the hypothesis.>

## Shape

<The rough form of a solution, explicitly non-binding.>
```

For `type: fix`, use:

```markdown
# <Title — the defect in one line>

## Symptom

<What misbehaves, as a user or operator sees it.>

## Where

<The surface, command, or package, as known.>

## Expected

<The behavior that should replace it.>

## Evidence

<A finding link when one exists; `none yet` is honest.>
```

For `type: perf`, use:

```markdown
# <Title — the cost in one line>

## Slow

<What is slow, for whom, and in which operation.>

## Measured

<The number that says so and how it was measured.>

## Target

<The number that would settle it.>
```

For `type: refactor`, use:

```markdown
# <Title — the tangle in one line>

## Tangled

<What resists change, and where it is duplicated or coupled.>

## Cost

<What it makes slow, risky, or wrong to touch.>

## Shape

<The structure that would replace it, explicitly non-binding.>
```

Keep `open` entries in `docs/backlog/`. When a Spec adopts an entry, set `status: promoted` and `spec` to that Spec's slug, then move the entry to `docs/specs/<slug>/references/`; git history remains the discovery trail. Set `status: declined` or `status: deferred` only with a non-null `reason`. The current type set is open: a new type must be a Conventional Commits type that expresses intent. Adding a type is a contract change that requires a corpus re-record, never an informal addition. Use `refactor` as the canonical token, never an abbreviation.

`docs/backlog/` holds unresolved `open` intent only. A `promoted` entry is adopted source material and moves to its consuming Spec's `references/` under the adoption contract; it is not a terminal implementation verdict. Every terminal Backlog Entry is deleted in the change that records its disposition under the retirement clause. An unknown status is a declaration error, never an inferred terminal disposition.

Keep evidence and intent distinct in both directions: a finding records what happened and is never a commitment; it is evidence-backed, immutable history. A backlog entry records what to do next and is never evidence. A finding may spawn a backlog entry; a backlog entry needs no finding. A `feat` entry is upstream raw material that the spec pipeline may consume, never the `write-idea` artifact itself.

Use this complete copyable Findings Operational Contract:

```markdown
---
status: pending # pending | partial | deferred | done | deprecated | superseded | closed | cancelled
created_at: YYYY-MM-DD
updated_at: YYYY-MM-DD
# waiting_on: <who or what it waits on, in one line> # optional, with since
# since: YYYY-MM-DD # optional, the date the wait began
---

# <Area> — <short title> (YYYY-MM-DD)

<Two to four sentences describing the session or investigation, the attempted outcome, and links to adjacent evidence.>

## 1. <Finding title — symptom, not hypothesis>

- Symptom / evidence: <observed behavior, command output, identifiers, and paths needed to reproduce>
- Root cause: <proven cause, or `unknown` with what was ruled out>
- Action / suggestion: <fix, mitigation, or route to a Spec, direct change, or upstream report>

## 2. <Next finding>

## What worked — keep

<Optional evidence about behavior worth preserving.>

## Addendum — YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>

<Append new evidence, root-cause proof, status context, or routing links without rewriting the original observation.>
```

A `pending` or `partial` Finding that waits on someone or something outside the repository may uncomment `waiting_on`, naming who or what in one line, and `since`, the `YYYY-MM-DD` date the wait began.

A Rollup is a Finding of `kind: rollup` that consolidates related Findings and shares their lifecycle contract. Only a Rollup with unresolved work belongs under `docs/findings/`; a terminal Rollup is deleted under the retirement clause. It declares a non-empty `members:` list of Finding basenames. Every member must resolve under `docs/findings/` or in Git. Use this extension:

```yaml
kind: rollup
members:
  - YYYY-MM-DD-<finding-slug>.md
```

A retirement deletes the file. A Finding, Rollup or Backlog Entry with a terminal status (`deferred` included), a handoff on the user's explicit confirmation, a finished Review Artifact, a rejected or deprecated ADR, a superseded ADR once an accepted successor names it with its date, and a Lesson Learned once an accepted ADR, a guide or a skill states what it teaches are deleted in the change that records the disposition. Git keeps the text. A Spec that absorbs a source adopts it and its Archive Record names it; any other retirement names its reason in the commit. A citation of a deleted file becomes the Git Locator `roundfix spec check` prints. The runtime's `roundfix history sanitize` removes what an earlier layout left.
Use `pending` when the finding is new and has no implementation Spec.
Use `partial` when a linked Spec covers only the selected implementation scope. Record the reason the remaining observations are unnecessary and link the covering Spec.
Use `deferred` only when the finding will not be implemented. Record the reason for deferral.

Set `status: done` as soon as the Spec is created and linked; do not wait for its Tasks, QA, archive, or release. Complete source adoption under the Spec's adoption contract. `done` records routing completion, not verified implementation; deletion follows the retirement clause.
Treat findings as immutable history: append evidence and routing links as dated addenda instead of rewriting the original observations.
Update `updated_at` whenever status changes or an evidence addendum is appended; keep `created_at` as the document creation date.

Triage resolves one pending cross-project message into exactly one Finding, one Backlog Entry, or one recorded discard. Preserve the boundary between evidence and intent: evidence never becomes intent without a human choice. A minted Finding or Backlog Entry must cite the message's provenance: the sending project, the message id and its date.

When a Finding's lifecycle closes, mint each typed Backlog Entry that its recorded actions call for, while preserving the boundary between evidence and intent. Where a fleet observation is captured before it reaches this repository is the cross-project continuity rule's concern, not this one's.

Before minting a Finding or Backlog Entry, including in Triage, look for an existing one that is not yet implemented and that the new observation or intent fits: an `open` Backlog Entry in `docs/backlog/` or an unresolved Finding in `docs/findings/`. Revise a fitting Backlog Entry in place under its existing name; extend a fitting Finding with a dated addendum, because a Finding is immutable history. Mint a new file only when none fits. A Triage that extends an existing entry resolves its message into that entry, which cites the message's provenance.

A Lesson Learned records something this repository tried, what went wrong, why, and what solved it. It is one file, `docs/lessons/YYYY-MM-DD-<kebab-slug>.md`, in this complete copyable form; keep each label as written and write the rest in the language of the repository's documentation:

```markdown
---
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
# <The lesson in one line>

- Context: <the work it happened in>
- Tried: <what was tried>
- Went wrong: <what was observed>
- Cause: <the proven cause>
- Solved by: <what solved it>
- Applies when: <when a reader should use this lesson>
- Does not apply when: <what looks alike and is different>
- Links: <the Finding, Spec, Pull Request or commit that holds the evidence>
```

Write a Lesson Learned only when every part of this test holds: something was tried, it went wrong, the cause is proven, something solved it, and no accepted ADR, reference document or glossary entry already states it. Otherwise write nothing. Apply the test at two moments: when a Finding closes, in the change that answers it or retires it, and when a Spec that needed a correction, a failed QA or a retry is archived. Write the file in that change, so the Pull Request that carries it shows the lesson to a person, who may delete it.
